Comparison

Omarchy vs CachyOS

Only what each project's official site says, with a source on every line.

Reviewed 2026-10-21 · independent editorial guide

Short answer

Built on Arch Linux, the Hyprland tiling window manager and the Quickshell desktop kit. CachyOS: Built on Arch Linux with the same rolling-release model.

Side by side

OmarchyCachyOS
BaseBuilt on Arch Linux, the Hyprland tiling window manager and the Quickshell desktop kit. [omarchy.org]Built on Arch Linux with the same rolling-release model. [cachyos.org]
PackagesSoftware comes from Arch's core, extra and multilib repos plus the Omarchy Package Repository; the AUR is optional. Install with omarchy pkg add <package>. [omarchy.org]Every package compiled for x86-64-v3, x86-64-v4 and Zen4 with LTO; core packages also get PGO and BOLT. [cachyos.org]
KernelNot a point the Omarchy manual compares.linux-cachyos kernel with a tuned scheduler, plus BORE, sched-ext, BMQ and RT options. [cachyos.org]
InstallerInstalls from an ISO, either full-disk or into free space next to another OS. Encryption is on by default. [omarchy.org]A graphical Calamares-based installer or a CLI installer. [cachyos.org]
DesktopKeyboard-driven Hyprland tiling desktop. Neovim is the default editor and Foot the default terminal. [omarchy.org]17+ desktops and window managers to pick at install, including KDE Plasma, GNOME, COSMIC and Hyprland. [cachyos.org]

More about Omarchy

  • Rolling release. New installs start on the stable channel, which follows an Omarchy Arch mirror kept one month behind the latest packages. [omarchy.org]
  • Secure Boot and/or TPM must be turned off in the BIOS to install. [omarchy.org]
  • Firewall on by default: all incoming traffic is blocked except LocalSend's port 53317, and SSH stays off until you enable it. [omarchy.org]
